messages:
Priya: Putting this thread up to capture the regional staged migration playbook. Goal: give customers a clear path to migrate model versions with minimal service disruption and a contractual soft-pin option for high-risk tenants. Need to agree on launch criteria, ownership, timeline, and AE talking points.

Alex: TL;DR proposal:
- Soft-pin: customer can pin a model version for up to configurable grace-window while we run a migration in their tenant.
- Staged multi-region rollout: canary -> regional ramp -> global cutover with explicit safety gates.
- Contract addendum: explicit rollback credits if regression passes predefined thresholds.

Jun: Metrics to gate on (suggested):
- Latency: median and p95 delta vs pinned baseline (median <= +10ms, p95 <= +25ms)
- Error surface: new 5xx or downstream failure types (alert if >0.2% increase)
- Quality: automated eval set pass rate (task-specific thresholds, e.g., >=95% baseline for retrieval; embed cosine drift <= 0.02)
- Customer-visible regressions: monitored via sampled human evals + alert if user complaint rate > baseline + 0.5%

Mara: Ops constraints: multi-region specifics matter. For customers with regional data residency we need:
- Region-scoped canaries (no cross-region traffic)
- A fail-open mode that preserves routing to pinned model in region if global config fails
- Quantized-only compatibility note: some on-prem kernels don't support BF16 -> if new variant is quant-only, we should treat as a separate SKU and require explicit customer consent.

Tess: Rollout cadence (ops proposal):
1) Dry-run (no prod traffic) - perf & smoke tests in staging
2) Region canary: 0.5% traffic for 2 hours -> 5% for 6 hours -> 20% for 12 hours
3) Regional hold: 48h monitoring window (heatmap checks + eval slices)
4) Cross-region roll for global customers: stagger regions by 12-24h
5) Full cutover after all regions pass
Automatic rollback triggers: p95 delta > configured threshold, increase in user-error rate above allowed bound, or eval A/B quality drop beyond threshold.

Sam: From product/commercial: we need two customer-facing options:
- Standard migration: no pin, default opt-out behavior, 7-day heads-up
- Soft-pin premium: customers lock version for X days, require SLA addendum, and pay for extended pinning. We should propose grace-window tiers: 30/60/90d. Also need language for credits and support response times.

Priya: Ownership: Jun owns bench spec and eval harness. Tess owns rollout policy + rollback playbook. Alex to own contractual language draft with Sam. Priya to shepherd RFC + stakeholder signoffs.

Jun: I'll publish benchmark slices covering chat long-context, retrieval-heavy queries, and embeddings drift by EOD Fri. Will include an automated harness that runs on canary traffic and emits a pass/fail signal.

OpsBot: scheduled-check: canary smoke test will run when Jun flips the deploy toggle. Will post metrics to the RFC channel.

Alex: Draft contract clause (starter):
"Customer may opt into a Soft-Pin for up to <GRACE_WINDOW>. During the Soft-Pin Redwood will run any scheduled model migrations for the customer's tenant against a staged rollout. If post-cutover automated benchmarks or customer-reported regressions exceed the mutually-agreed thresholds, Redwood will either (a) roll back to the pinned model version or (b) issue service credits as defined in the addendum."

Mara: Edge cases we should capture in RFC:
- Tenant with multi-region routing & mixed hardware (GPU/CPU fallback)
- Models with external dependencies (search indices, vector DBs) that need coordinated migrations
- Customers using deprecated tokenizer variants or custom adapters

Sam: AE one-pager items: short summary, grace-window options + pricing, rollback SLA, what triggers credits, expected timeline for region-by-region migration, and a quick FAQ about quantized variants. I'll draft and share.

Priya: Timeline: internal RFC early next week, stakeholder review midweek, ship beta of soft-pin flow + canary tooling in 6 weeks. If no objections, I'll book the RFC. Post any other asks here (e.g., legal constraints, platform hooks).

Jun: Quick technical note: bench harness will expose per-slice baselines. We should make thresholds overridable per-tenant (org-level flags) to support large enterprise customers.

Tess: We'll add a canary ops runbook that includes a manual 'fast kill' play button and an automated fallback path. Also will document alert runbooks for the SRE rotations.

Priya: Thanks. If everyone agrees drop :rocket:, otherwise flag concerns.
